notes: Eligible. Original 2014 ChemComm communication from the AIST group (Xu), with ESI. I1: H2 uptake isotherms at 77 K up to about 1 atm (Fig. 5a) and H2 uptake values for C800, NC800, BNC800-1, BNC800-2 (Table S1, 1.8, 1.7, 1.4, 1.7 wt% at 77 K) are the paper's own results; the ESI says isotherms of 'nitrogen and other gases' were measured on BELSORP max / BELSORP mini II automatic volumetric adsorption equipment, so the method is volumetric. The ESI does not name H2 in that sentence; H2 is inferred to be among the 'other gases'. I2: C800 is an undecorated carbon (MIL-100(Al) calcined at 800 C and HF-washed); NC800 (14.8 wt% N) and BNC800-1/-2 (N 11.5 / 8.1 wt%, B 2.3 wt% in BNC800-1) are N- and BN-decorated carbons, described as graphitic carbons; C800 alone satisfies I2. I3: 77 K and 1 atm stated in text; Fig. 5a x-axis is Pressure (P) 0.0-1.0 with no unit printed (read as atm from the text). I4: BET areas by N2 at 77 K for the same samples (C800 2731, NC800 2397, BNC800-1 1068, BNC800-2 1522 m2/g, Table S1; ESI Section 1: relative pressure 0.05-0.20). I5: English. Not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in text). Not a review; no statement that the H2 values were published before. Quote note: the PDF text layer drops the minus sign in unit exponents, so 'g-1' appears as 'g 1' in the quotes; the page images show g-1. The text layer interleaves the two page columns, so each quote was taken from one column.
